moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
learningObjectives: Retrieve a specific item using TestData - Find & provide item and ActionMode Constraint.
Use {TDS[ResourceName.PropertyName]} with the retrieved item's alias.
Update a known item through its alias using TestData - Update item.
Move a retrieved item to another type using TestData - Move item to type.

elements.description: Retrieves a previously created record via a search query. The 'Existing TDS type*' field defines which dataset to search (e.g. CustomerDetails).
Restricts the search to records matching a specific condition — e.g. TDS attribute Status = 'New', to find only newly registered customers rather than any customer record.

elements.text: Existing TDS type chooses the search scope. Alias name identifies the retrieved item during the TestCase, not a search condition; if omitted in Find, the type name is used as its default.

bulletPoints: Existing TDS type* = which dataset to search. ActionMode Constraint = which record(s) within it.

elements.description: Use {TDS[ResourceName.PropertyName]} in the Value field after finding or creating the item. ResourceName identifies the item by its alias, followed by the attribute name. Do not substitute the repository name or an arbitrary type name.

Independent example: Find an item of type CustomerDetails with alias customer, then use {TDS[customer.Email]} to access its Email attribute. If Find instead omitted the alias, the default would be CustomerDetails, making {TDS[CustomerDetails.Email]} valid for that retrieved resource.

bulletPoints: {TDS[ResourceName.PropertyName]} — resource alias, then attribute, separated by a dot.

elements.description: Changes a known item's attributes through its alias. A usual workflow first finds the intended item, then supplies the alias to Update item; an item created earlier can also have an alias. Define changed attributes under Data structure with ActionMode Input.

Existing alias name (item) must identify the item already available to the TestCase. For an explicit alias customer, pass customer; only an omitted Find alias defaults to the type name. A synthetic Status change from New to Active is an explicit test-data update.

elements.text: An application-side change is not itself a TestData Update item operation. Verify the application's expected state and explicitly maintain the repository data when the workflow requires it.

bulletPoints: Update uses a known item's alias; a type name alone does not identify an arbitrary item.

elements.title: Application state and test-data state are separate
items: Find a synthetic order item and assign the alias order.
Perform and verify the intended operation in the application under test.
If required, explicitly Update the order item's Status in TDS.

elements.description: This is an independent practice example, not a verified Academy payment walkthrough. Keep the application's state assertion separate from the repository update, and handle failures before marking test data consumed. A generic successful HTTP response does not prove a business operation completed.

elements.text: Do not treat an application response as evidence that TestData - Update item has run.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Moving consumed records to a new TDS type

elements.description: Once the full order process (including payment) has run, that customer's data is considered consumed. Moving it into a distinct TDS type keeps the repository stateful — it's immediately clear which records are still 'live' and which have already been used, which is especially valuable for a distributed team.

Moves a known item identified by Existing alias name (item) into Existing or new TDS type. With alias customer, pass customer and destination CustomerDetails_Used. The alias need not equal the source type. One move targets one known item, not every item in the source type.

bulletPoints: Existing alias name (item) identifies the retrieved item; Existing or new TDS type specifies its destination.

elements.text: 📄 Exercise 03A-03G (Retrieve Test Records, Update Test Records, Add Items to the Shopping Cart, Purchase Items, Process Payments through Non-UI, Process Purchase Order, Move used records to other TDS type) — Official Tricentis Academy course material, not redistributed here. Access it inside the official course.

examPitfalls.title: Updating without an identified item
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting Update item to choose an arbitrary target from a type name.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pass the alias of an item found or created earlier; use Input for changed attributes.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming application changes update test data
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating an application-side result as evidence that the test-data update ran.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Verify the business result and explicitly update the known test-data item when required.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing item alias and type
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Putting a source or destination type name into the item alias field when the item has a different alias.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the known item's alias and configure its destination separately.

examPitfalls.title: Using the wrong resource expression
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using TD instead of TDS, reversing alias and attribute, or using a colon separator.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use {TDS[ResourceName.PropertyName]} with the retrieved item's actual alias.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test has retrieved a CustomerDetails item with the explicit alias customer. Which expression accesses its Email attribute?
practiceQuiz.hint: Use TDS, the resource alias, a dot and the attribute name.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The explicit alias is customer, so the documented expression is {TDS[customer.Email]}.

optionExplanations.A: The resource alias must precede the attribute; Email is not this item's alias.
optionExplanations.B: TDS accesses the Email attribute of the resource identified by customer.
optionExplanations.C: The syntax separates resource and attribute with a dot, not a colon.
optionExplanations.D: The documented Test Data Service command is TDS, not TD.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester adds TestData - Update item to change Status, but has not identified an item or supplied its alias. What is missing?

options.text: Nothing — Update item chooses a target automatically.
A known item found or created earlier, identified by Existing alias name (item).

practiceQuiz.hint: The update needs a known item, not just a type name.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Existing alias name (item) identifies an item already available to the TestCase. Changed attributes use Input.

optionExplanations.A: The module needs the target item's alias; it does not choose an arbitrary item.
optionExplanations.B: Finding or creating an item supplies the alias required to address it later.
optionExplanations.C: Constraint filters a search; it is not an Update task value.
optionExplanations.D: Repetitions changes execution count, not the identity of the target item.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A synthetic order test verifies that the application has changed the order's state. Does that assertion alone prove that the separate TDS item's Status was updated?

options.text: Yes, TDS always mirrors backend status changes instantly.
No — explicitly update the identified TDS item if the test-data workflow requires the new state.
Only if Repetitions is set to 1.

practiceQuiz.hint: Application verification and a TestData update are different operations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A successful application assertion does not execute TestData - Update item. Maintaining the separate item's state requires the appropriate explicit test step.

optionExplanations.A: There is no automatic mirroring implied by verifying an application result.
optionExplanations.B: An explicit update maintains the known test-data item's attributes.
optionExplanations.C: Execution count does not configure state synchronization.
optionExplanations.D: Processing can be stored as a Status attribute value; it is not forbidden by TDS.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester has found one CustomerDetails item with alias customer and wants to move it into CustomerDetails_Used. Which value goes in Existing or new TDS type on Move item to type?
practiceQuiz.hint: Configure the destination type separately from the item alias.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The destination is CustomerDetails_Used. Existing alias name (item) is customer, not the source type CustomerDetails.

optionExplanations.A: CustomerDetails is the source type, not the requested destination.
optionExplanations.B: CustomerDetails_Used is the destination configured for this move.
optionExplanations.C: New is a sample status value, not the destination type.
optionExplanations.D: Processing is a sample status value, not the destination type.

quickRecap.value: TestData - Find & provide item; type and Constraint scope the search; alias identifies the retrieved resource.
TestData - Update item — known item alias, changed attributes with Input.
Application verification is not a test-data update; explicitly maintain TDS state when required.
Move item to type — known item alias identifies the item; Existing or new TDS type specifies the destination.
